lessons: Criterion 2 and the Scope-in edit to test_callers_pass_the_current_release are contradictory. They require pyproject 1.9.0 to select 2.0.0, but the ticket's own formula f"{parts[0]}.{int(parts[1]) + 1}.0" gives 1.10.0. No version maps to any <major>.0.0.

Fix the ticket: in tests/unit/test_roadmap_release_boundary.py, rename the fixture heading `### 2.0.0` (line 22) to `### 2.1.0`, keep pyproject version "2.0.0" (line 60), and assert `next: n-nine`. Update criterion 2 and Scope-in to match.

Keep the rest of criterion 2: pyproject "1.0.0" passes "1.1.0" to choose(). In that test, change `calls == ["1.0.0"]` (line 78) to `["1.1.0"]`. Check that the test_current_release cases (0.3.0, 0.3.1 -> 0.4.0; 0.6.1 -> 0.7.0; 2.10.4 -> 2.11.0) agree with the formula. They do.

Lines 33-34 of that file also pass "2.0.0" directly to choose() with the 1.0.0/2.0.0 fixture. Those cases never call current_release, so they can stay. List them in Context so the fixture heading rename keeps them consistent, or rename their release argument along with the heading.

Before resubmitting, run `uv run clutch ticket lint roadmap-align-pypi-versions-r2` and `uv run clutch ticket review roadmap-align-pypi-versions-r2`. Recheck every version example in the ticket against the formula, since minor+1 never rolls over to the next major.
